steps: Cover soybeans with water, and soak overnight or at least 12 hours.
Remove hulls by rubbing beans between both hands.
Wash away or skim most hulls using a skimmer or strainer. A few remaining hulls do not affect quality.
Cook beans until just tender, not mushy; undercooked is best for tempeh.
Drain beans, and spread to dry somewhere with airflow.
Collect beans into a bowl and mix in cider vinegar to acidify and inhibit unwanted organisms.
Sprinkle tempeh starter over the beans and mix well.
Pack loosely into banana leaves, zip-lock bags or shallow dishes. Puncture bags at roughly 1 cm (½ inch) intervals to supply oxygen.
Put into an incubator, preferably on racks permitting air circulation. An electric oven with its light on provides a little heat.
Incubate about 12 hours at 30–35°C (86–95°F) with a heat source unless the ambient temperature is already that hot.
After 12 hours remove or turn off the heat source; the fermenting beans generate their own heat and may overheat.
Monitor periodically and remove when fluffy white tempeh completely covers the beans with no gaps.
Use immediately in a tempeh recipe, refrigerate for two to three days, or freeze up to two months.

ingredients: Cookies: 3 eggs, reserving one for glazing
Icing: 150 g or more powdered sugar
steps: Combine cookie ingredients except one egg in a bowl and mix into a smooth dough.
Beat the reserved egg in a cup or small bowl.
Divide dough into 5–6 portions. Roll one portion to about 3 mm thick.
Cut shapes with cookie cutters and transfer to a parchment-lined baking sheet.
When the sheet is full, glaze the cookies with beaten egg.
Bake at 180°C for a few minutes until light brown.
Repeat with remaining dough.
Mix icing egg white and powdered sugar to make icing, adding sugar if not firm enough.
Put icing into a piping or plastic bag and cut a hole about 1 mm wide in the tip.
Squeeze to pipe icing and decorate the cookies.

ingredients: 2 cups (450 g / 16 oz) white granulated sugar
1 cup (325 g / 11.5 oz) liquid honey (any variety)
steps: In a 3–4-quart (2.8–3.8 L) heavy-bottomed saucepan, combine sugar, salt and cornstarch until uniform.
Stir in honey and water using a wooden or metal spoon. Heat over medium-high heat, stirring continually until sugar dissolves.
Continue stirring until boiling, then cook undisturbed to 270°F/132°C (soft crack stage). Add butter.
Remove from heat and pour onto a greased lipped cookie sheet, greased marble slab or silicone mat.
When cool enough to handle with clean greased hands, stretch, fold and recombine until light-colored with a satiny gloss. Pull continuously for 10–15 minutes, preferably with a friend.
Roll into ½-inch ropes and cut into 1-inch-long pieces using a knife or greased scissors. Wrap pieces in squares of waxed paper and twist the ends.
